newsitem.title: UK: Panamaxes favour owners in London freight.
newsitem.headline: Panamaxes favour owners in London freight.

text.p: The market, except in Capers, generally continued to favour owners, especially in the Panamax category.

This was despite the tricky situation in the Mississippi with an OBO aground near New Orleans, barges adrift in the river and other factors interfering with grain exports. There is an upswing in Panamax activity from S America with grain, and in the Indian Ocean and Far East, principally in minerals. A strong feature of the latest market has been the volume of period chartering of Panamaxes. the BFI rose 12 points to 1515.

There are said to be 20 vessels waiting in Paranagua to load 908,000 tonnes soyabeans and another 20 to load 648,000 tonnes meals: grain shipments from Brazil are rising following a good crop and the abolition of export taxes. This sitation together with active chartering from Argentina has underpinned the Atlantic market for Panamaxes and Handies.

Andre booked Mare Vikingo 64,155 dwt delivery Lisbon early April for 5-7 months at $11,350/11,400 daily plus $250,000 bonus if redelivery Far East, and Cabral were linked with Minoan Sky 54,424 dwt delivery Med for short period business on private terms. Dreyfus conceded a firm $13.00 to Kardamyla for 52,000/5 heavy grain Paranagua/Mississippi with options including $17.00 to the Continent, itself another stronger rate. Otherwise the main grain chartering activity concerned Handies for s America, but few fixtures were released.

A rate of $21.50 upwards was rumoured paid by Cargill for 18/20,000 heavy grain Rio Grande/Casablanca for early April, and Andre fixed 25,000 maize Up River/Cape Town for early April at $20.50. Nan Fung 34,995 dwt and Boris Livanov 23,940 dwt were both said to be fixed from this area. The most striking rate reported was $16.00 agreed by Tradigrain for Nordmoritz for 54,000 heavy grain NoPac/Taiwan for 4/11 April - a clear illustration of the state of the Far East Panamax market.

Three weeks ago Continental booked Mass Enterprise in this trade at $13.85. New grain business quoted today included Becker with 30,000 maize Up River/Seaforth April/May, the Canadian wheat board with 23/25,000 wheat Vancouver or Prince Rupert/Sri Lanka option Mozambique, and showa for a vessel of 30/33,000 dwt delivery Nopac 10/25 April for a trip to Japan.

Caper rates continued soft in the Atlantic. Some of the latest fixtures were being kept private - Leopardi 131,000 dwt, for example, open Ijmuiden end-March was rumoured covered for transatlantic business by British Steel, and Pantelis A Lemos 144,348 dwt may have fixed Intercorp with coal from Bolivar to Rotterdam. China Prosperity 151,000 dwt was linked with NYK for ironore from Narvik or Brazil to Kemaman, but details are lacking. In the Panamaxes UBT paid a firm $16,000 daily for Giovanni Bottiglieri 75,265 dwt delivery Black Sea prompt trip Far East, but the main action in these sizes was in the East with a fair number of vessels booked for period timecharter.

Halla were said to have agreed $12,250 daily for the newbuilding Fearless for 18 months, the GIC-relet Anangel Venture 69,406 dwt was reported taken by Yukong delivery Japan early April for 2-3 months at $12,500 daily, and there were reports that the Goldbeam-relet Pasquale Della Gatta 73,000 fixed delivery Muscat for 3-5 months at about $13,250/13,500 daily (possibly to NSAC). Perhaps relatively the strongest period rate of all was conceded by T K Boesen for the 1981-built Petra 64,848 dwt delivery passing Muscat 5/10 April for 6-8 months at $11,650 daily - the same as fixed by Yukong with this vessel yesterday which failed on subjects.
Trip fixtures included a firmer $13,500/13,750 daily reported paid by MOSK for the Halla-relet Capitano Giovanni 74,500 dwt delivery prompt Japan for an E Australian round.

Business back to the Continent was said to have been concluded by Medmar with Lia 64,675 dwt delivery prompt Far East AT $7,500 daily, and Royal Accord with coal from Roberts Bank to Rotterdam for 1/15 April at $13.90/14.00.
